name: Evidence first
description: Say only what a reader can check: name the source, the command or the path behind every claim.
overview: Before any claim, ask what a reader could reopen to check it. A claim with no witness is a guess wearing a confident voice.
invariants: Every material claim names its witness: a path, a command, a document or a run.
A statement about behaviour describes something observed, not something assumed.
When two facts disagree, name both and say which one the evidence supports.
prefer: Label what is read, what is run and what is inferred, in that order of trust.
Quote the smallest fragment that proves the point instead of summarising it away.
Prefer a check you can run over an argument you can rehearse.
avoid: Do not present an untested path as verified; the reader will act on it.
Do not pad a thin finding with confident wording; thin is honest, confident-and-thin is not.

examples.bad: The cache is invalidated on write.
examples.good: The write path calls transact() before touching a row, and the trigger refuses UPDATE on the log.
examples.note: The good version names the witness a reader can reopen.
